clue.text: Near a record player, book collection by expert

indicators.note: by means beside, so the book collection sits next to the expert

parts.note: a disc jockey, DJ, is someone who plays records
an ace is an expert
NT, the New Testament, is a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: Somewhere close by, a DJ spins records while an expert sorts through a library.
explanation.definitionFit: Something adjacent lies next to or close by, a synonym for near.

clue.text: Snake a fellow gets wife to cut tail off?

parts.note: to snake is to wind, as a road winding along

indicators.note: the wife is set to cut into the fellow, splitting him open

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: A man whose wife chops off a snake's tail, in some grim fable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snake' reads as a noun but is the verb wind. 'to cut' puts W inside DON.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind down is to dwindle gradually towards a stop, much as things tail off.

clue.text: Excellent papers put before extremely gullible old president

indicators.note: the earlier pieces are placed in front of the letters that follow

parts.note: cool is slang for excellent
ID, identity documents, are one's papers

indicators.note: extremely asks for the extreme letters, the first and last, of gullible

explanation.surface: Fine documents are pushed in front of a naive former head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives GE, the outer letters of gullible.
explanation.definitionFit: Calvin Coolidge was the thirtieth US president, serving in the 1920s.

clue.text: No one perfect, including leader of Tories, on reflection, is rash

indicators.note: on reflection means the whole assembly is read backwards, as in a mirror
including means the Tories' leader is taken inside the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
pure means perfect, unblemished

indicators.note: leader of asks for the first letter of Tories

explanation.surface: Nobody is flawless, not even the Conservative leader, when you think it over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' puts T into NOIPURE to give NOITPURE; 'on reflection' turns that round. 'rash' reads as hasty but is the skin outbreak.
explanation.definitionFit: An eruption is an outbreak of spots on the skin, which is what a rash is.

clue.text: Scrap book that people use for addresses

parts.note: a scrap is a fight, and to box is to fight
Numbers is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A fight over a book, the kind people turn to when addressing letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' suggests discarding, but here it is a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Box numbers are post-office box references people use as postal addresses.

clue.text: Priest taking an age to pen final letter

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the age encloses the final letter

parts.note: an era is an age
Z is the final letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A clergyman takes ages to write the last letter of his correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' reads as write, but means enclose here.
explanation.definitionFit: Ezra was an Old Testament priest and scribe who led returning exiles.

clue.text: Answer given by woman about queen rejected previously

indicators.note: about means the woman goes round the other piece

parts.note: a lady is a woman

indicators.note: rejected means the queen's letters are turned back

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the queen

explanation.surface: A woman replies after a queen has been turned down earlier on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' signals the turnaround of the queen's letters, and 'about' sets them inside the woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Already means by this time or beforehand, a close synonym of previously.

clue.text: Generally free

definitions.meaning: as a whole, as in the public ...
not captured, as an escaped prisoner still on the loose

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both in general and roaming free, uncaught.

clue.text: Old rabbit coming back up to scratch

indicators.note: coming back means the word for chatter is read in reverse

parts.note: to rabbit, in British slang, is to chatter, as is to yak

explanation.surface: An elderly bunny returning to good health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rabbit' is British slang for chattering on; 'coming back' signals the turnaround. The furry animal is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Okay means acceptable or satisfactory, which is what up to scratch means.

clue.text: Chip in counter, bit needing replacement

indicators.note: the letters need to be replaced, put back in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gaming counter with a chipped bit has to be replaced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chip' and 'counter' set a gambling scene, but 'Chip in' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To contribute is to add one's share, which is what chipping in means.

clue.text: Chap disrespectfully damaging instrument? Flipping drivel!

parts.note: the viola is a stringed instrument

indicators.note: flipping means turning the word for nonsense over, back to front

parts.note: rot is drivel, nonsense

explanation.surface: Someone wrecks a musical instrument, and the exasperated speaker dismisses it all as nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild curse but turns ROT into TOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A violator is a person who breaches or desecrates something without respect.

clue.text: Sacrifice featuring in short book with Latin translation

indicators.note: translation means the letters are converted into a new form, rearranged
short means the word for book loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Latin version of a little book that deals with sacrifice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts BOOK to BOO; 'translation' then rearranges BOO plus LATIN.
explanation.definitionFit: An oblation is an offering made to a god, a religious sacrifice.

clue.text: Jack's following increased in sporting arena

indicators.note: following means the jack's word comes after the other

parts.note: rose means increased, went up
the jack is the small target bowl in the game of bowls, and the apostrophe s stands for is

explanation.surface: Jack's fan base has grown, as seen at a sports ground.
explanation.walkthrough: In bowls, a British lawn game, the jack is the small ball players aim at. 'Jack' looks like a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rose Bowl is a famous American football stadium in Pasadena, a sports venue.

clue.text: Drink one daughter ordered with meal

indicators.note: ordered means the letters are arranged into a new sequence

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A daughter orders a drink to go with her meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like asking a waiter, but rearranges ONE, D and MEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Lemonade is a soft drink flavoured with lemon.

clue.text: Score — kick ball endlessly after game

indicators.note: after means the trimmed ball comes after the game

parts.note: to kick a habit is to drop it
Go is an ancient board game

indicators.note: endlessly means the ends of ball are removed, leaving its middle

explanation.surface: Someone scores by kicking a ball after the match has started.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kick' sounds like football but means give up, as with a habit.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop goal is a rugby score made by drop-kicking the ball over the bar.

clue.text: Top sporting association

indicators.note: to top is to cut off the head, so the word for flirting loses its first letter

parts.note: sporting means frolicking or flirting, which is dalliance

explanation.surface: A leading sports organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' reads as an adjective meaning best, but is a verb telling you to behead DALLIANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance is a union or partnership formed for mutual benefit.

clue.text: After vacations embattled dignitary will have to circulate

indicators.note: after vacations means once the words are emptied of their insides, only the outer letters remain

explanation.surface: Once the holidays end, a beleaguered official must mingle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacations' looks like holidays but means emptying: ED and DY remain.
explanation.definitionFit: An eddy is water or air swirling round, so to eddy is to circulate.

clue.text: Speaker's cute expression millions overlooked

definitions.note: the apostrophe s stands for is: the speaker is the answer

parts.note: twee means excessively cute

indicators.note: overlooked means millions are left out of the expression

parts.note: a term is an expression, a word or phrase

explanation.surface: A sweet phrase from the Speaker ignores millions of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speaker' suggests the House of Commons chair but is a loudspeaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A tweeter is a small loudspeaker that reproduces high-frequency sounds.

clue.text: Feared churchman's home is inside capital close to border

definitions.note: the apostrophe s stands for has

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: inside means the word is goes within the capital

parts.note: Quito is the capital of Ecuador

indicators.note: close to means the last letter of border

explanation.surface: A dreaded cleric lives in a capital city near the frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: An inquisitor was an officer of the Inquisition, a dreaded church interrogator.

clue.text: Husband I wrote about possesses unknown sort of gun

indicators.note: possesses means the rearranged letters hold the unknown inside
about means the letters are moved around into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
Z is an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: A husband says he wrote about owning a mysterious type of firearm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges I WROTE into OWITER, and 'possesses' puts Z inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A howitzer is a short artillery gun firing shells at high angles.

clue.text: Overwhelm woman in order to stop current meeting

indicators.note: to stop means to plug a gap, so the nun is set between the other pieces

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
a date is a meeting
a nun is a woman in a religious order

explanation.surface: A woman is told to halt the meeting going on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'current' looks like present, but is I, the physics symbol for current.
explanation.definitionFit: To inundate is to flood or swamp, so overwhelm with a mass of something.

clue.text: Commitment initially doubled to supply a drug

indicators.note: the initial letter is doubled in value: Roman D, 500, becomes M, 1000

parts.note: dedication is commitment

explanation.surface: A pledge doubled at the outset so as to provide medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: In Roman numerals D is 500 and M is 1000, so doubling the initial D makes it M.
explanation.definitionFit: Medication is a medicine, a drug given to treat illness.

clue.text: Vole originally entering wild area for juicy plant

indicators.note: entering means the reworked rodent goes inside the reworked area
wild means the letters run riot into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: originally here means in an original, novel way, so the letters take a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A vole first ventures into wilderness looking for a succulent plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally' (in a novel way) rearranges the rodent's letters, 'wild' rearranges the area's into A...ERA, and 'entering' sets one inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Aloe vera is a succulent plant whose thick leaves hold soothing gel.

clue.text: Get excited again being back 'ome

parts.note: the rear is the back
the dropped h marks a Cockney home, a house said as 'ouse

explanation.surface: Someone gets worked up again on returning home, in a Cockney accent.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, drop their h's: home is 'ome, so house is 'ouse.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearouse is to stir up or excite once more.

clue.text: Canadian area — never-ending terrain boy visits

indicators.note: visits means the boy goes into the cut-down terrain
never-ending means the word for terrain loses its last letter

parts.note: land is terrain
Bert is a boy's name

explanation.surface: In a region of Canada, a boy roams across endless country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'never-ending' trims the final letter of the terrain word, and 'visits' sets the boy inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An Albertan is a native of Alberta, a province of Canada.

clue.text: Number of fans fail to find opening page

parts.note: the gate is the number of spectators at a match
to fold is to fail, as a business folding

explanation.surface: A crowd count fails to show up on the front page.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' looks like the start, but is a page that opens out.
explanation.definitionFit: A gatefold is an oversized page folded in that the reader opens out.

clue.text: Where film may be enjoying repeated success

definitions.meaning: camera film comes wound on a spool

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers film wound on a spool and a run of consecutive wins.

clue.text: Kind of rock found in part of Wales briefly

indicators.note: briefly means the county's name is cut short, abbreviated

parts.note: Glamorgan is a historic county of south Wales

explanation.surface: A type of stone discovered in a corner of Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: GLAMORGAN is a historic county in south Wales; 'rock' suggests stone but means music.
explanation.definitionFit: Glam is a flamboyant, glittery style of 1970s rock music.
